unsupported_forms: Employee delegation, universal schema, or nested-group semantics (handoff row I06): only the dedicated account and the configured resolver are claimed; nesting is supported only through the Active Directory in-chain resolver and is unsupported for OpenLDAP
Application entitlement taxonomy: a directory group is a fact, and what it permits stays with the application

Authentication other than the simple bind over LDAPS or StartTLS (anonymous or unauthenticated bind, an unprotected simple bind, every SASL mechanism, the Active Directory Sicily mechanism, LDAPv2): only one arrangement is admitted
Shared directory accounts: one directory account per agent, the default of identity-mapping section 5, and a workload with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error
A distinguished name, cn, uid, sAMAccountName, user principal name, mail, or display name as an identifier: only the unique id (entryUUID or objectGUID) is admitted

A directory other than OpenLDAP 2.6 or Active Directory Domain Services (for example Active Directory Lightweight Directory Services, another LDAP server, a cloud directory): no documentation for them was read
Nested groups on OpenLDAP, dynamic groups, and any other overlay-based expansion: nesting is configured as unsupported and a requirement on the nested path ends in UNSUPPORTED_REQUIREMENT
Membership through the Active Directory primary group, through tokenGroups, or across domains and forests: the direct and chain resolvers do not claim them

Reads served by a replica or by a domain controller other than the one that takes changes, with no declared bound: no replication bound is published, and without a declared bound every finite limit is unachievable
Referral chasing, and truncated results treated as complete: a referral or a limit-exceeded result is never a complete answer
Any route other than the reference route of protected_routes: not listed, so not claimed

residual_limits: Post-read: stock data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later removal from a group or a disable, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation, directory: the 0 second bounds of freshness hold for one server that takes every change and answers every read, with no cache; elsewhere a removal, disable, or lock reaches the gateway within the bound the deployment declares, and PACT does not promise instantaneous revocation from a replicated directory; lock state diverges between servers (OpenLDAP records failures on the replica that served them, Active Directory replicates a lockout urgently only to the PDC emulator and some sites and does not replicate an unlock urgently)

Revocation propagation, enrollment: a revocation or compromise mark reaches the gateway within the 0 second status bound of the registry, inside the consistency of the registry backend; the in-memory backend is local to one process

Session age: a deployment that authenticates once and keeps a session carries the age of the login in the principal fact; groups and state are read for each evaluation, so a stale session cannot claim a fresh group observation

Directory enforcement: the adapter reads state attributes and cannot show that the directory enforces them (for example that an OpenLDAP database loads the password policy overlay); the bind result is the directory's own enforcement

Access control uniformity: the visibility sentinel detects a lookup account that lost access to a whole base, not an entry-specific denial inside a base, which can only remove a group or hide an account and so yields FAIL, never a positive result

Directory reads are not re-stamp checked: each read is a new source record with its own as-of instant, so the monotonic guard never compares two reads of one entry; it still protects relayed or re-signed copies

Lock expiry: whether a lapsed temporary lock clears pwdAccountLockedTime or resets the computed Active Directory lockout bit is not established, so a lapsed lock can be reported as locked, which fails closed
